342929.title: The interval conjecture for second-level universal lower bounds
342929.statement:
For each dimension $n$, let $D(n,\tau)$ and $D(n,\tau+1)$ be the endpoint cardinalities associated with consecutive levels, and consider those $N$ in the interval

$$
N\in [D(n,\tau),D(n,\tau+1)]
$$

for which second-level bounds exist.

**Interval conjecture.** For every dimension $n$, the values $N\in [D(n,\tau),D(n,\tau+1)]$ for which second-level bounds exist form an interval.

The conjecture concerns the observed organization of second-level universal lower bounds across cardinalities; the source formulates it as a concluding conjecture and provides examples, but no resolution.
342929.analysis: Source v2 Conjecture 6.1 is the exact interval assertion. The quadrature/interpolation ULB-space conditions are not merely one continuous inequality. No monotonicity of all feasibility conditions in N proved; local continuity cannot exclude disconnected feasible components. Primary concluding passage read, not all quadrature proofs or journal corrections.

343145.title: The independence-number bound for clique immersions
343145.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. **Independence-number clique immersion conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains

$$
K_{\lceil n/\alpha(G)\rceil}
$$

as an immersion.

This conjecture extends Vergara's conjecture from independence number $2$ to arbitrary independence number. The bound is motivated by the inequality $\chi(G)\ge \lceil n/\alpha(G)\rceil$ and would follow from the immersion analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture; current results provide weaker lower bounds.
343145.analysis: Source v4 Conjecture 4 is the exact clique immersion bound. The metadata solved remark refers to chromatic t<=7, not all n/alpha. Chromatic lower bound does not produce an immersion unless the stronger immersion-Hadwiger conjecture is supplied. No edge-disjoint routing for general alpha. Journal DOI acquired as metadata only.

343223.title: Condensed Ricci curvature conjecture for strongly regular conference graphs
343223.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a strongly regular conference graph with parameters

$$
(4\beta+1,2\beta,\beta-1,\beta)
$$

where $\beta\geq 2$. **The condensed Ricci curvature conjecture.** The condensed Ricci curvature satisfies

$$
\Bbbk(x,y)=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\beta}
$$

for every edge $xy\in E$. In particular, every strongly regular conference graph has positive condensed Ricci curvature strictly greater than $\frac{1}{2}$. The conjecture is expected to follow from the matching criterion in the cited theorem if the neighbor sets of every adjacent pair admit perfect matchings; the paper states that this is left for future work.
343223.analysis: Bonini et al. Conjecture 1.7 is proved by Chen-Liu-Zhang arXiv:2409.06418v3 (12 Feb 2026), Theorem 1.4. Their kappa is Lin-Lu-Yau curvature, equal to the source condensed curvature by idleness a=1-epsilon. Substitute gamma=beta, d=2beta, alpha=beta-1 into (2+alpha)/d=(beta+1)/(2beta). General Hall proof and special beta2..6 proof passages read. This is exact public resolution, not a new Paley-only result.

343360.title: Common minimal-tree conjecture for totally real algebraic integers
343360.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\in\mathtt{TRAI}\setminus\{0\}$. For each $\lambda_i$, let $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_i}$ denote the set of trees having a nowhere-zero $\lambda_i$-eigenvector.
**Common minimal-tree conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_1}\nsubseteq\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_2},\qquad
\bigcap_{i=1}^{k}\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{min},\lambda_i}\neq\emptyset.
$$

The conjecture asserts both that the first two minimal-tree families are not nested and that one tree can be minimal for all the specified nonzero eigenvalues. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
343360.analysis: Literal noncontainment fails for equal lambdas, and even for distinct lambda,-lambda. Every tree is bipartite. Multiplying an eigenvector by +1 on one part and -1 on the other changes eigenvalue lambda to -lambda, preserving nowhere-zero coordinates. Applying twice proves Tmin,lambda=Tmin,-lambda. Thus the first conjunct fails at 1,-1. This is an ineligible source-domain correction. Common intersection for arbitrary nonzero specified eigenvalues remains unpaid; no glued-tree nowhere-zero eigenvector construction proved.

343451.title: The regularity conjecture for graphs with bounded edge-ideal regularity
343451.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal, and let $G^c$ denote its complement. **Regularity conjecture for graphs with bounded edge-ideal regularity.** If

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G))\leq 3
$$

and $G^c$ has no induced $4$-cycle, then

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G)^s)=2s
$$

for all $s\geq 2$. The source presents this as a related conjecture and records that analogous stabilization results are known for several graph classes; the stated general case remains open.
343451.analysis: Source Conjecture 4.3 exact. Its own dunce-hat flag-no-square construction has reg(I)=3 and reg(I^2:ab)=3 for every edge: read source discussion explaining why the naive colon-ideal induction does not settle reg(I^2)=4. A colon upper bound of 5 is insufficient and does not refute 4. Journal/citing updates not cleared.

343625.title: Existence of uniform posets that are not monoid posets
343625.statement:
A **uniform poset** is a poset such that, for every pair of elements $x,y$, the principal upsets ${\uparrow\hspace{-1.5pt}} x$ and ${\uparrow\hspace{-1.5pt}} y$ are order-isomorphic.

**Uniform-poset nonexistence conjecture.** There are uniform posets that are not monoid posets.

Uniformity generalizes the auto-equivalent setting, and the supplied context says that auto-equivalent posets are uniform. The existence of a uniform poset outside the class of monoid posets is presented as a suspicion and remains open in the supplied text.
343625.analysis: Source Conjecture 6.5 exact. Finite uniform posets are antichains: a maximal element has singleton upset, hence so does every element; antichains are monoid posets via a group with the trivial submonoid. Infinite transitive layered digraph construction is suggested in source, but absence of a group Cayley representation does not exclude a monoid representation. Need an obstruction to the endomorphism-monoid characterization, not just nonvertex-transitivity. Source definitions/proof characterization not fully audited.

343681.title: Thomassé's cycle-reversion conjecture for dichromatic number
343681.statement: Let $D$ be a potentially infinite digraph. A **cycle reversion** reverses the edges of a directed cycle; iteratively perform such reversions, requiring that each edge is reversed only finitely many times, and denote the resulting reorientation by $D^{*}$. **Thomassé's conjecture.** It is possible to choose the reversions so that the dichromatic number of $D^{*}$ is at most two. The conjecture concerns reducing the dichromatic number of arbitrary finite or infinite digraphs through controlled cycle reversions, and its status is open.
343681.analysis: Source v2 Theorems 1.8 and 7.2 assert exact arbitrary-cardinality cycle-reversion result, each edge reversed only finitely often. RS(D) is the source reversion-sequence notion. Section7 proof reduction and Lemma7.3 transfinite construction read; auxiliary lemmas not all independently rebuilt. Rename D triangleleft C as D*; the source theorem directly supplies every requested quantifier. No finite-only transfer needed.

343937.title: Balogh, Kostochka and Treglown's conjecture on degree sequences forcing perfect clique tilings
343937.statement:
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r$ dividing $n$. Suppose that $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with degree sequence $d_1\leq\ldots\leq d_n$ satisfying the following conditions:

$$
d_i\geq (r-2)n/r+i\quad\text{for all }i<n/r;
$$

$$
d_{n/r+1}\geq (r-1)n/r.
$$

**Balogh, Kostochka and Treglown's conjecture.** Then $G$ contains a perfect $K_r$-tiling, that is, a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_r$ covering all vertices of $G$.

This conjecture seeks a degree-sequence condition forcing a perfect $H$-tiling that is best possible in a weaker sense than a Chvátal-type condition. It concerns the degree-sequence analogue of perfect clique-tiling results and remains open in the supplied source context.
343937.analysis: Exact finite degree-sequence perfect clique tiling is stronger than an asymptotic additive-error tiling theorem. A maximal partial tiling need not leave vertices whose degrees inherit the original sorted indices. No absorbing/exchange proof meeting both sharp inequalities. The r=1/n indexing issue is an ineligible endpoint correction; no such correction counted. Source largely introductory/conjectural passages only.

343967.title: Duality conjecture for entropic complexity of access structures
343967.statement:
Let $P$ be a participant set, let $\mathcal A\subset 2^P$ be an access structure, and let $\mathcal A^\bot$ denote its dual access structure. Let $\sigma(\mathcal A)$ denote the entropic complexity of $\mathcal A$. **Duality conjecture.** For every access structure we have

$$
\sigma(\mathcal A)=\sigma(\mathcal A^\bot).
$$

The analogous equality is known for the polymatroid and linearly representable complexities, while the corresponding statement for entropic complexity is described as a long-standing open problem. The source explicitly says the conjecture is probably not true, so this conjecture is refuted.
343967.analysis: Source Conjecture1 explicitly remains a complexity duality question. The phrase probably not true is not a refutation. Source warns that refuting ideal-dual closure does not refute equality of infimal complexity: nonideal can still have infimum1. Need separated entropic complexity bounds for an exact access structure; polymatroid duality alone insufficient.

344067.title: The lattice equivalence conjecture for facial weak order
344067.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a hyperplane arrangement and let $B$ be a base region of $\mathcal{A}$. Write $\operatorname{PR}$ for the poset of regions and $\operatorname{FW}$ for the facial weak order.

**Lattice equivalence conjecture.** The poset of regions $\operatorname{PR}$ is a lattice if and only if the facial weak order $\operatorname{FW}$ is a lattice.

The forward implication is established in the paper; this conjecture asserts the converse for arbitrary hyperplane arrangements and base regions.
344067.analysis: Complete interval-poset retraction bridge in ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md. Source Proposition2.5 supplies facial intervals, Definition2.9 supplies coordinate order; Theorem4.1 supplies PR lattice => FW lattice. If FW is a lattice, join of singleton region intervals must itself be singleton: its lower endpoint is already a region upper bound and minimality collapses endpoints. Dual for meets. This resolves the literal equivalence by a complete routine order-theoretic adaptation, 0 credit; source author PDF404 leaves current author/journal comparison unread, not a novelty claim.

344114.title: Bang-Jensen et al.'s Meyniel-type conjecture for strong digraphs
344114.statement:
Let $D$ be a strong digraph on $n$ vertices. For vertices $u,v$ of $D$, write $d(u)$ and $d(v)$ for their total degrees. Suppose that $u$ and $v$ are non-adjacent and have a common out-neighbour or a common in-neighbour.

**Bang-Jensen et al.'s conjecture.** If

$$
d(u)+d(v)\ge 2n-1
$$

for every such pair $u,v$, then $D$ is hamiltonian.

This conjecture is presented as a strengthening of the classical Meyniel theorem. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

Strong connectivity alone does not supply a cycle factor. No longest-cycle insertion route handles nonadjacent pairs lacking common neighbors.

344371.title: K6 and K6,6 sequence rank formula for four-dimensional rigidity
344371.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph and let $F\subseteq E(K_n)$. A proper $\{K_6,K_{6,6}\}$-sequence is the sequence construction defined in the source using copies of $K_6$ and $K_{6,6}$; write $C_{\leq t}$ for the union of its edge sets. **Four-dimensional rank conjecture.** The rank function of ${\cal R}_{4,n}$ is

$$
r(F)=\min\{|F\cup C_{\leq t}|-t:(C_1,\ldots,C_t)\text{ is a proper }\{K_6,K_{6,6}\}\text{-sequence in }K_n\}
$$

for every $F\subseteq E(K_n)$. The conjecture is motivated by the failure of unique maximality for ${\cal R}_{4,n}$, and the source gives no resolution.
344371.analysis: Source journal-form Conjecture8.2 is exact R4,n formula, distinct from the established C21 cofactor rank formula in dimension3. A circuit-count upper bound alone cannot prove equality/free elevation maximality. No lower-rank certificate for every F; no symbolic matrix or computation run.

344477.title: Characterization of the tableaux-graph order by row entries
344477.statement: Let $S,T\in\mathcal{T}(n,n)$ be standard Young tableaux of shape $(n,n)$, and let $a_i$ and $b_i$ denote the entries in the first row of $S$ and $T$, respectively. **Characterization conjecture.** If $a_i\geq b_i$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$, then $S\leq T$ in the tableaux graph. Together with the preceding implication proved in the paper, this would characterize the tableaux-graph order by coordinatewise comparison of first-row entries. The supplied text presents this as part of the proof of the main conjecture and gives no resolution status beyond that presentation.

Row membership encodes Dyck paths; coordinatewise top-entry decrease is generated by DU->UD. This is the standard dominance/order-ideal cover construction, with every tableau validity and termination bridge proved. Source Conjecture3.7 kept distinct from positive-transition-matrix Theorem3.9. No claim of significant new theorem or worldwide first proof.

344495.title: Compact DV representations for GIRS matrices
344495.statement:
Let $(A,\mathbb{G})$ be a GIRS-$c$ pair, and let $\mathbb{V}_\mathbb{G}$ denote the vertex set of $\mathbb{G}$. A **DV representation** is a representation with rank parameters $r_i$ indexed by the vertices. **Compact DV representation conjecture.** If $(A,\mathbb{G})$ is GIRS-$c$, then $(A,\mathbb{G})$ possesses a DV representation with

$$
r_i\leq 2c
$$

for every $i\in\mathbb{V}_\mathbb{G}$. The preceding discussion motivates compact representations, but the source gives no evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.
344495.analysis: Source v3 Conjecture2 is compact DV r_i<=2c for every vertex, not the overlapping-Hankel O(N^2) algorithm Conjecture1. Existing line/cycle constructions do not give common compatible rank spaces for arbitrary graph cuts. Large general matrix realization does not control every local r_i. 344596.title: De Loera et al.'s Ehrhart positivity conjecture for matroid polytopes
344596.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid, and let $\mathscr{P}(M)$ denote its basis polytope. Its Ehrhart polynomial is the polynomial counting lattice points in integer dilations of $\mathscr{P}(M)$. **De Loera et al.'s conjecture.** The coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of $\mathscr{P}(M)$ are positive. This conjecture was posed for matroid basis polytopes and is motivated by Ehrhart-positivity questions in combinatorics. The paper proves the assertion for all hypersimplices, which are the basis polytopes of uniform matroids; the general matroid case is not resolved here.
344596.analysis: Ferroni arXiv:2105.04465v3 (7 Mar2022), Theorems1.5/5.3, supplies a rank9 sparse paving matroid on20 elements. Nonbases are 9-subsets whose sum of zero-based indices is0mod20. 344621.title: The multiple-free subset-sum conjecture for powers of two
344621.statement:
Let $z\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\subseteq[2^z]$, where $[2^z]=\{1,2,\ldots,2^z\}$. For each non-empty subset $A_i$ of $A$, write $S(A_i)$ for the sum of its elements. **Multiple-free subset-sum conjecture.** If for every $i,j\le 2^k-1$ the quotient

$$
\frac{S(A_i)}{S(A_j)}
$$

is not a power of $2$, then

$$
k=z+O\left(1\right).
$$

The condition says that the subset sums form a multiple-free sequence with respect to powers of $2$. The conjecture is motivated by numerical data and would sharpen the known lower-bound constructions for this problem; the paper does not provide a proof or resolution.

Literal i=j gives quotient1=2^0, so quantification must exclude identical subsets; equality k=z+O(1) also must concern extremal size rather than every tiny A. These wording fixes receive0. Distinct-pair upper-bound reading still needs removal of log k loss from odd-part packing; source Theorems3/4 do not do this.

344727.title: The symmetric chain decomposition extension conjecture for hypercubes
344727.statement: A **symmetric chain decomposition** (SCD) of the hypercube $Q_n$ is a partition of its vertices into symmetric chains, where a symmetric chain is a path $(x_k,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_{n-k})$ such that $x_i$ lies at level $i$ for every $k\leq i\leq n-k$. **The symmetric chain decomposition extension conjecture.** Every SCD can be extended to a Hamilton cycle in $Q_n$. This conjecture extends results of Streib and Trotter and the Greene–Kleitman construction, which show that particular SCDs can be extended to Hamilton cycles. It is motivated by the conjecture of Ruskey and Savage that every matching in $Q_n$ extends to a Hamilton cycle.
344727.analysis: Source Conjecture4 asks EVERY SCD extends to Hamilton cycle. Its proved Greene-Kleitman construction concerns one selected SCD. Contracting chains gives a quotient whose Hamilton cycle is not established, and endpoint adjacency does not follow from arbitrary matched levels. No general splicing invariant. n1 cycle convention is an ineligible endpoint omission.

344799.title: Criticality conjecture for interlacing edges of large Schrijver graphs
344799.statement: Let $d$ be any integer, let $k_d$ be a threshold depending on $d$, and let ${\rm SG}(2k+d,k)$ be the Schrijver graph. An edge is **interlacing** according to the standard interlacing-edge definition for Schrijver graphs, and an edge is **critical** if deleting it lowers the chromatic number. **Interlacing-edge criticality conjecture.** For every $d$ and every $k>k_d$, all interlacing edges of ${\rm SG}(2k+d,k)$ are critical. This would characterize the critical edges for Schrijver graphs of large size with fixed small chromatic-number excess, extending the corresponding theorem cited in the source; the full characterization of critical edges is not known.
344799.analysis: Source final Conjecture1 exact fixed d/eventually all k. Established d2 critical-edge description does not supply general d. Single edge noncritical at a small k cannot refute eventual quantified claim. Need infinitely many k for one fixed d, or a uniform (d+1)-coloring after edge deletion. No such construction supplied.

344808.title: The three-weight sum-set characterization for odd sums
344808.statement:
Let $C(\Omega)^\bot$ be a code of length $n$ with three nonzero weights $w_1<w_2<w_3$, where $p$ is prime and $m$ is a positive integer. The weights are related to an $s$-sum set $\Omega$ as in the paper.

**The three-weight sum-set conjecture.** $\Omega$ is an $s$-sum set for some $s>3$ if and only if

$$
(w_1,w_2,w_3)=\left(w_1,n(p-1)p^{m-2},2n(p-1)p^{m-2}-w_1\right),
$$

for some $0<w_1<n(p-1)p^{m-2}$.

This claim characterizes the three-weight configurations that can arise from an $s$-sum set with $s>3$, extending the preceding results that identify a symmetric weight configuration yielding $s$-sum sets for every odd $s>1$. The supplied text does not indicate whether the claim has been proved or disproved.
344808.analysis: Exact source Conjecture1 concerns one s>3. Theorems7/9/10 give spectral criterion, symmetric sufficiency and at most one exponent for nonsymmetric triple; the last does NOT exclude one exponent. $$
\operatorname{Mod}^{\pm}(S).
$$

Schmutz Schaller proposed this conjecture for the automorphism group of the curve graph, and the paper resolves it for all but the cases $(g,p)=(1,3)$ and $(g,p)=(0,5)$, so the general statement remains open in those exceptional cases.
